mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2% over the preceding month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-trend period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the CPIAUCSL exceeds +2%, the expected inflation path shifts right, prompting the market to discount future equities more aggressively and producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: IC for this signal is > 0.05 over a 60-day window during an inflation spike, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in PAYEMS exceeding +1% in a month signals tight labor markets, prompting firms to invest more in capital and raise expected earnings, which elevates S&P 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not higher than the prior 10-day average during the same tightening episode (rolling mean p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 grows by more than 5% in a quarter, it indicates robust consumer demand that supports corporate earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative during the quarter with the GDPC1 surge (comparing to the prior 20-day period).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below 100 (index) for two consecutive months suggests weakening manufacturing capacity, which reduces growth expectations and produces negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 30-day expansion phase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 2020-01-01 historical averages of 152k and 3.6% respectively indicate a labor market in transition, creating uncertainty that depresses S&P 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly worse than during the pre-transition period (rolling IC > 0.03 over 60 days).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of FEDFUNDS below 1.5% and no upward trend, the market expects future rate cuts, which lowers the real discount rate and supports S&P 5-day forward returns.
regime_hint: very low policy rate with no upward bias
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not higher than the 5-day average during the previous 30-day period of similar policy conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS falls by more than 10% in a month, it reflects weak demand absorption in the retail sector, lowering growth expectations and resulting in negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than during the prior 30-day period of normal absorption (rolling IC > 0.03).
